land.text: Cyrene and Cyrenaica, 'awarded' to Ptolemy VIII by Roman intervention; Ptolemy VI kept Egypt and Cyprus

predecessors.note: The ptolemaic-kingdom dossier records the 163 loss with the slug cyrenaica as counterpart; this is the state it means. Cliopatria's Cyrenaica row has no shape for 247-111.

land.text: Cyrene, rejoined to Egypt and Cyprus when the Alexandrians called on Ptolemy VIII to return from Cyrene in 145

successors.note: The ptolemaic-kingdom dossier has the matching gain at 145.

capitals.name: Cyrene (Shahhat)
capitals.note: The page speaks of Cyrene as the seat: Ptolemy VIII left a governor there and the Alexandrians called him back 'from Cyrene'.

rulers.name: Ptolemy VIII Physcon
rulers.title: king of Cyrene
rulers.note: The lead infobox gives his reigns in Egypt as 170-164 and from 145; between them he held Cyrene.

correction.text: Cyrene and Cyrenaica as Ptolemy VIII's separate kingdom

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria's Cyrenaica row has no shape between 248 and 111 (the Ptolemaic Kingdom shape of 164-127 is 679,560 km2 and holds Cyrenaica inside it); the later Cyrenaica shape of 110 (116,347 km2) is used as the best outline. The page gives no area.

ledger.note: 163 BCE: Rome gives Cyrene to Ptolemy VIII. 'As a result of Roman intervention, Ptolemy VIII was awarded control of Cyrene, Libya'; 'a pair of Roman agents convinced Ptolemy VI to grant Ptolemy VIII control of Cyrenaica'. He had been 'expelled in turn in 163 BC' from Alexandria after driving out his brother in 164; the award's year is the page's context, not its sentence.
163 BCE: Cyrene and Cyrenaica pass from Ptolemy VI's kingdom to Ptolemy VIII.

region.text: Cyrene, held by the rebel governor Ptolemy Sempetesis

ledger.note: 162 BCE: a revolt at Cyrene. 'Ptolemy Sempetesis, the governor that Ptolemy VIII had left in charge of Cyrene in his absence, suddenly raised a revolt.'
162 BCE: 'He regained control over Cyrene by the end of 162 BC'; the page does not say whether by negotiation or force.
161 BCE: Ptolemy VIII invades Cyprus, which the Romans had promised him; Cypriot resistance forced him to abandon it after up to a year (the ptolemaic-kingdom dossier reads the page the same way).
160 BCE: the Cyprus expedition is abandoned (the page dates the expedition 161).
154 BCE: Ptolemy VI besieges his brother on Cyprus. 'Ptolemy VIII was besieged by his older brother at Lapethus and was captured'.
154 BCE: Ptolemy VIII withdraws from Cyprus. He 'was persuaded to withdraw from Cyprus, in exchange for continued possession of Cyrenaica'.
145 BCE: Ptolemy VIII returns to Alexandria and Cyrene rejoins Egypt. After Ptolemy VI's death on campaign, 'the Alexandrians called on Ptolemy VIII to return from Cyrene'.
145 BCE: the separate kingdom of Cyrene ends. Ptolemy VIII's will of 155, 'in which he bequeaths Cyrenaica to Rome' if he died without children, did not take effect.

wars.name: Ptolemy VIII's Cyprus expeditions
wars.outcome: The first (161) failed against Cypriot resistance; in 154 Ptolemy VI besieged him at Lapethus and he left Cyprus 'in exchange for continued possession of Cyrenaica'.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for Ptolemy VIII's Cyrene.

sources.title: Ptolemy VIII Physcon
sources.note: The 163 award of Cyrene, the Sempetesis revolt (162), the Cyprus expeditions (161, 154), the 155 will, the 145 return.

notes: One page (budget 1-2). The page has Ptolemy VIII's reign at Cyrene by context, not by a sentence giving 163 with Cyrene; the 163 date is the expulsion year on the page and the award follows it. Same-year contest pair against a rebel governor (162). The 161 and 154 Cyprus fights duplicate the ptolemaic-kingdom dossier's contests, which use cyrenaica as counterpart; the ptolemaic-kingdom dossier should name cyrene-under-ptolemy-viii (or this dossier's counterpart should be changed to cyrenaica if the orchestrator prefers the Cliopatria slug). Ptolemy Apion's separate kingdom (105/101-96) is in the cyrenaica dossier. Not opened: the Cyrenaica or Magas pages (me-05-a).
